name: My Chess Family – Chess Puzzles and Advent Calendar
author: mychessfamily

sections.description:
Put two free chess activities for children on your site: a chess advent calendar for December and a chess puzzle of the day all year round. Children solve each puzzle by moving the pieces on the board. Good for school, club, library and family websites.

The chess advent calendar

  • 24 doors, one opening each day from 1 December, by the date in the UK.
  • Every door has three puzzles: Elf (easy), Reindeer (medium) and Santa (hard).
  • Before December there is a practice door, and a count of the sleeps until door 1.
  • No peeking: a door’s puzzles only arrive on its day.
  • Stars for solved puzzles, remembered in the visitor’s own browser.

The chess puzzle of the day

  • A new puzzle every day, with a short hint.
  • Tap or drag a move. A wrong move goes back; “Show me” plays the answer with arrows.

Made for children

  • No sign-up, no adverts, no cookies, no tracking.
  • No chat and nothing for anyone to type.
  • Every puzzle is checked by a chess engine to make sure it has one clear answer.
  • Works with a finger on tablets and phones, and with a mouse.

The puzzles come from My Chess Family, a child-safe chess learning site for families in the UK. A new door or puzzle needs no plugin update.

External services

This plugin shows puzzles from My Chess Family (https://mychessfamily.uk), run by the plugin’s author. It cannot work without it.

When a page with the block or shortcode is viewed, the visitor’s browser asks mychessfamily.uk for the puzzles: https://mychessfamily.uk/chess-advent-calendar.json for the advent calendar and https://mychessfamily.uk/puzzle-of-the-day.json for the puzzle of the day. This happens each time the page loads. No cookies are sent or set and the plugin sends no information about the visitor. As with any web request, the visitor’s IP address reaches the server, and browsers normally send your site’s address. My Chess Family counts these requests by the site they came from, keeps nothing about the visitor, and does not track anyone.

  • Terms of use: https://mychessfamily.uk/terms
  • Privacy notice: https://mychessfamily.uk/privacy

Credits

  • Puzzles from the Lichess puzzle database (CC0).
  • Chess pieces by Colin M.L. Burnett (cburnett), used under the GPL.
  • chess.js by Jeff Hlywa (BSD 2-Clause licence).
  • The words and pictures served with the puzzles are © My Chess Family (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0).
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. In the block editor, add the Chess advent calendar or Chess puzzle of the day block. Choose a skin in the block’s settings.
  3. Or use a shortcode in any post, page or text widget:
    [chess-advent] or [chess-puzzle-of-the-day].
    Both take a skin: [chess-puzzle-of-the-day skin="snow"] (snow, gingerbread, candycane, forest, space or contrast; the puzzle of the day also has plain). On the calendar, children can pick another skin themselves.
sections.faq:
Is it free?

Yes. Both are free, with no sign-up, no adverts and nothing to buy.

What ages is it for?

Children who know how the pieces move, from about 5. The advent calendar’s three levels go from easy (Elf) to hard (Santa), which suits confident players and grown-ups.

Does it collect any data?

No. It sets no cookies and stores nothing about your visitors. Which doors a child has solved is kept in their own browser only. See “External services” below for what the browser asks My Chess Family for.

What does the advent calendar show outside December?

From November it shows this year’s calendar, with the practice door until 1 December. After Christmas all the doors stay open to play.

Can I use it on a classroom whiteboard?

Yes. It works on any screen size.
